Raymond III was born around 1140 in the County of Tripoli. He was the eldest son of Raymond II and Hodierna. He inherited the countship after his father died in 1152. His early years were spent learning the duties of a noble lord in a frontier state. He received training in warfare and diplomacy from his mother and his advisors. *Political Career*
Raymond III ruled the County of Tripoli from 1152 until his death in 1187. He sought to maintain independence while navigating the shifting alliances of the Crusader states. He often negotiated with the Kingdom of Jerusalem to secure mutual support. He also engaged in diplomatic contacts with Muslim leaders such as Nur ad Din and later Saladin. He attempted to balance tribute payments with military readiness. He participated in the defense of Tripoli during several raids. He supported the rallying of Crusader forces after the fall of Jerusalem in 1187. He tried to coordinate a relief effort but his forces were unable to prevent the defeat at Hattin. After the battle he retreated to Tripoli and prepared for a possible siege.

*Later Years*
In the years following 1187 Raymond III faced increasing pressure from Saladin's forces. He worked to strengthen the fortifications of Tripoli. He sent envoys to Europe to request aid. He hoped that a new Crusade would relieve the pressure on his county. Despite his efforts the situation grew dire. He fell ill in early 1187 and died shortly thereafter. His death marked the end of an era of relative autonomy for the County of Tripoli. His successors would eventually lose the territory to the Mamluks in the thirteenth century.

*Legacy*
Raymond III is remembered as a capable ruler who tried to protect his people during a difficult time. He is noted for his diplomatic skill and his attempts to forge alliances across religious lines. His reign illustrates the challenges faced by the Crusader nobility in the twelfth century. Historians view him as a figure who embodied the struggle between survival and idealism in the Outremer.
